probes.question: When the options were framed as deaths instead of lives saved, which treatment did most people pick?
True or false: in the Asian disease problem, the two framings described different outcomes.

image.alt: A half-full glass of water on a sunlit cafe table.

body.question: A deadly disease threatens 600 people. Treatment A: 200 people will be saved. Treatment B: a 33% chance that all 600 are saved, a 66% chance that no one is. Which did most people choose?
body.reveal: 72% chose Treatment A. But when the same outcomes were framed as deaths (A: 400 people will die; B: a 33% chance no one dies, a 66% chance all 600 die), 78% chose B. Same facts, flipped choice: the framing changed the decision.
